ai.description: *Nyctibatrachus robinmoorei* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and pale yellow belly. It is distinguished by its pointed snout and prominent, fleshy, finger-like toe tips.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus robinmoorei* is best distinguished by its unique, vibrant orange-red coloration on the inner thighs and groin, which is absent in other similar night frogs.
ai.habitat: *Nyctibatrachus robinmoorei* inhabits the wet evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 800 and 1,100 meters.
ai.behavior: Robin Moore's Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small invertebrates along the mossy, spray-drenched rocks of its stream-side habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus robinmoorei* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs on wet rocks that undergo direct development into froglets.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus robinmoorei* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, specifically inhabiting mid-to-high elevation streams in the Wayanad region.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Nyctibatrachus robinmoorei* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes emitted from rocky stream habitats.
